title: How Lila Sciences and Anyscale Scaled GLM-5.3-Flash Training to 1M tokens | Anyscale
gist: Anyscale's SkyRL team and Lila Sciences trained the open hybrid-attention MoE model GLM-5.3-Flash on 1M-token sequences using 64 B200 GPUs, 64x longer than the stack initially supported, with all changes open-sourced in SkyRL and some upstreamed to Megatron-LM. Fine-tuning on the human genome at 512k tokens cut held-out loss 4.8% in 80 steps, with the biggest gains on tokens with the most preceding context.

insights.claim: The authors argue scientific data such as genomes, protein or RNA sequence families, and multi-day experiment records loses essential structure when cut into a few thousand tokens, and closed-loop autonomous-lab AI accumulates contexts of hundreds of thousands of tokens.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: AI-for-science creates structural demand for long-context training compute beyond typical chat workloads.
insights.quote: Scientific data is long by nature.
insights.locator: Scientific data is long by nature.

insights.claim: Many open models advertise 1M-token context but may lack out-of-the-box performance on target tasks at that length, requiring training on the task's own data at full length.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Advertised context windows overstate usable capability, creating a market for long-context fine-tuning infrastructure.

insights.claim: Lila Sciences and Anyscale trained GLM-5.3-Flash at 1M tokens per sequence on 64 B200 GPUs, 64x longer than the training stack could handle at the start.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Demonstrates million-token post-training is feasible on a modest 64-GPU cluster with open tooling.

insights.claim: A 1M-token sequence fits in 144.5 GiB per GPU, under the B200's 178 GiB, with throughput of 13.7k tokens/s at 1M and a peak of 24.9k tokens/s at 256k on 64 B200s.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Quantifies the memory headroom needed for long-context training, relevant to HBM-rich GPU demand.

insights.claim: At 1M tokens, CPU-offloaded layer inputs reach about 180 GB per GPU before context parallelism, over 1 TB per 8-GPU node, so host memory must be planned alongside GPU memory; pinned memory copies were 22% faster than pageable.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Long-context training raises host DRAM requirements per node, a tailwind for server memory content.
insights.quote: Plan host memory, not just GPU memory.

themes.theme: Engineering lessons for hybrid MoE models

insights.claim: GLM-5.3-Flash is a hybrid model with 34 of 45 layers using Kimi Delta Attention linear attention and 11 using DeepSeek Sparse Attention, plus a 4x wider residual stream and MoE layers, each requiring separate memory work.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Shows Chinese open-model architectural innovations being adopted in Western AI-for-science pipelines.

insights.claim: GLM's sparse attention layers silently fell back to dense attention because fused kernels only accepted DeepSeek's exact tensor shapes, using 114 GiB per GPU at 16k and failing at 32k; padding tensors halved memory.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Kernel-compatibility fragility in open models is a hidden cost that favors teams with deep infrastructure expertise.
insights.quote: Nothing raised an error; the run simply used 114 GiB per GPU at 16k and ran out of memory at 32k.

insights.claim: Sparse attention moves rather than removes quadratic cost because selecting 2,048 tokens per query requires scoring every query against the full sequence; chunking and splitting that scoring across GPUs made the training step 2.1x faster at 256k.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Sparse attention does not eliminate long-context compute scaling, sustaining demand for accelerators.
insights.quote: Sparse attention moves the quadratic cost; it doesn't remove it.

insights.claim: Every memory fix costs throughput: CPU offloading cut peak memory at 256k from 142 to 98 GiB but added 21% to step time, so each technique is enabled only at the length that requires it.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Long-context training cost scales super-linearly as memory-saving tricks erode throughput.

insights.claim: Random-token benchmarks underestimate MoE memory because real text routes unevenly; on a real long-context dataset the busiest GPU received about 4x the average tokens and 512k ran out of memory where random runs fit.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Cluster sizing based on synthetic benchmarks risks underprovisioning for real MoE workloads.
insights.quote: Test memory on real data before sizing a cluster.

insights.claim: In RL runs with real weights, the trainer's log-probabilities matched vLLM's within 0.04 to 0.07 mean absolute difference from 128k to 1M tokens, and an overfit test drove loss from 1.65 to 0.17 in 20 steps.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Correctness validation supports credibility of long-context RL training on open stacks.

insights.claim: Post-training on chromosomes 1 and 2 of the hg38 human reference genome at 512k tokens per sequence reduced held-out loss on unseen chromosome 22 by 4.8% in 80 steps.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Early evidence that general LLMs can be adapted to genomics, relevant to AI-for-biology companies.

insights.claim: Loss improvement was largest on late-position tokens with up to 500k tokens of preceding context, which the authors argue proves the model learned to use long context rather than only local patterns.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Validates long-context training as yielding real capability gains, not just longer inputs.
insights.quote: That last part is the evidence that it learned to use long context, not just local patterns.

insights.claim: All experiments ran on Ray managed by the Anyscale platform on a 64-GPU B200 cluster in Lila's cloud, with SkyRL using Ray to coordinate training and inference workers, and the recipe released open source in SkyRL with fixes going upstream to Megatron-LM.
insights.speaker: Anyscale / Ray
insights.so_what: Case study supports Anyscale's positioning as the orchestration layer for frontier-scale RL and post-training.
